title: Grateful Dead Live at Roosevelt Stadium on 1973-08-01
lineage: source 1: SBD>MR>R>R>D>CD>EAC>SHN; source 2: SBD>MR>C>D>CD>EAC>SHN; source 3: AUD>MR>C>C>C>CD>EAC>SHN

ai_review.summary: A stellar 8/1/73 show with a legendary Dark Star→El Paso→Eyes→Morning Dew sequence captured in a well‑balanced matrix mix.
ai_review.review: The performance is highlighted by Jerry’s birthday fire, an unforgettable Dark Star that morphs into a high‑energy El Paso and a soaring Eyes of the World, ending with one of the most revered Morning Dew jams.  The recording blends soundboard clarity with just enough audience ambience to feel present, though occasional early glitches and a muddy bass low‑end keep it from being flawless.

ai_rating.rationale: Consistently glowing comments about the musical performance (70% weight) plus generally good but not perfect recording quality (30% weight) across many reviews yields a strong overall rating.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Crisp, well‑balanced mix of board and audience; early set has minor glitches and occasional audience patches; some listeners note the bass can be muddy and a few moments sound muffled.

show_quality.setlist_flow: The set flows seamlessly, with a monumental Dark Star that transitions into an energetic El Paso, then a spacious Eyes of the World and a haunting Morning Dew.  The second set is praised as “amazing” and the birthday atmosphere adds extra excitement.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Repeatedly lauded for his sizzling birthday guitar work, leading four consecutive tunes and delivering a memorable solo throughout the Dark Star/El Paso/Eyes/Dew stretch.
band_member_comments.Phil: Praised for driving the pre‑verse jam on Dark Star with “galactic” bass runs; several reviewers note his mix is more forward this night.
band_member_comments.Bob: A few comments call Bob’s playing “whacked,” but overall he is recognized as integral to the band’s sound.
band_member_comments.Keys: Keith’s keyboard fills are described as fantastic, adding cool touches in choruses and complementing Jerry’s lead work.
band_member_comments.Drums: Bill Kreutzmann’s drums are louder than usual, delivering a punchy, crisp feel that many reviewers highlight as a positive change.
